Done. The task is complete after a single execution.

**What was produced**

- `out/T3/solution.py` loads the 160-tensor input, casts the 48 projection matrices matched by an anchored regex to bfloat16, drops the 12 `h.<i>.attn.bias` mask buffers, and keeps all other tensors float32.
- All four required checks run before any file is written, and the script exits non-zero if one fails.
- Sharding is greedy in key order with a 64 MiB budget on tensor data. Tensors over the budget go alone in their own shard.

**Output layout in `out/T3/`**

| Shard | Tensors | Tensor bytes |
|---|---|---|
| model-00001-of-00004.safetensors | 59 | 66,259,968 |
| model-00002-of-00004.safetensors | 58 | 66,256,896 |
| model-00003-of-00004.safetensors | 30 | 40,983,552 |
| model-00004-of-00004.safetensors | 1 (`wte.weight`) | 154,389,504 |

The index file maps all 148 tensor names to these shards and records the total size.

**Report** was written to `out/T3/REPORT.md` with one execution, no failures, and the pitfalls noted. The only unclear point in the task was the shard naming scheme, so I used the HuggingFace convention.
